result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Full Time 
Remuneration: $117, 745.00 - $147, 664.00 
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM30440
 

About the Opportunity

South Western Sydney Local Health District (SWSLHD) invites applications from motivated Advanced Trainees in Paediatrics for a 12-month rotational position, comprising six months in General Paediatrics with a perinatal component at Campbelltown Hospital and six months in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at Liverpool Hospital. Accredited by the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP), this position is ideal for Advanced Trainees pursuing a career in General Paediatrics or Neonatal and Perinatal Medicine. This position offers a great opportunity to develop advanced clinical skills across neonatology and general paediatrics within two busy teaching hospitals that provide care to one of the largest, fastest-growing, and most culturally diverse communities in New South Wales. 

Where You'll Be Working

Campbelltown Hospital is a contemporary teaching hospital with an expanding paediatric service delivering comprehensive inpatient, emergency, ambulatory and outpatient care to infants, children and adolescents. The department provides a supportive and collaborative learning environment with a diverse case mix, allowing trainees to gain valuable experience across acute general paediatrics, neonatal medicine through the Level 4 Special Care Nursery and multidisciplinary models of care. 

Liverpool Hospital is a major tertiary referral and teaching hospital with a Level 5 Neonatal Intensive Care Unit providing specialist care for premature and critically unwell newborns from across South Western Sydney and surrounding regions, offering trainees extensive exposure to complex neonatal care within a multidisciplinary team. 

As part of SWSLHD, both hospitals are committed to excellence in patient care, education, research and innovation, providing trainees with access to structured teaching and a strong culture of learning and professional development.

What You'll Be Doing

As an Advanced Trainee, you will work as an integral member of multidisciplinary teams across both rotations, providing high-quality, evidence-based care to neonates, infants, children and their families. At Campbelltown Hospital, you will broaden your experience in general paediatrics through the management of acute and chronic paediatric conditions across inpatient, emergency and ambulatory settings, while working closely with consultant paediatricians and multidisciplinary teams. During your rotation at Liverpool Hospital NICU, you will develop advanced neonatal skills in the assessment and management of premature and critically unwell newborns, including attendance at high-risk deliveries, neonatal resuscitation, intensive care management and family-centred care under the supervision of experienced neonatologists. Throughout the rotation, you will participate in structured education, clinical governance, quality improvement and teaching activities, contributing to a culture of continuous learning while building the knowledge, skills and confidence required for a successful career in neonatology or general paediatrics.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

Registered with the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) as an Advanced Trainee (or equivalent). Applicants registered with the RACP must have outstanding Advanced Training requirements as at February 2027. Please outline your remaining training requirements in your application

Demonstrated knowledge and clinical competence in the contemporary assessment and management of acute paediatric and neonatal conditions, including sound clinical judgement, neonatal resuscitation, common paediatric procedures, and an awareness of the limits of own experience.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively within a supervised clinical environment, prioritise competing clinical demands, provide safe and timely patient care, and deliver accurate clinical documentation and handover.

Demonstrated high-level communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with patients and families, work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, adapt communication to different audiences, and manage challenging interactions or differing clinical opinions professionally.

Demonstrated commitment to patient safety, quality improvement, clinical governance, and the supervision and teaching of medical students, junior medical officers and other health professionals. Please provide an example of your teaching experience and commitment to professional development.

Demonstrated computer literacy and the ability to work effectively in a computerised clinical environment

Need more information?

 2) Find out more about applying for this position
For role-related queries or questions, contact Christine Peng at Christine.Peng@health.nsw.gov.au

result.description:
Flexiforce Australia is seeking Process Workers to join our team on both day and afternoon shifts at our clients Moss Vale NSW facility. This is a casual position with full-time ongoing hours that play a vital role in our clients manufacturing and assembly operations. As a Process Worker, you will be instrumental in ensuring production lines run smoothly and efficiently, directly contributing to the quality of products and the success of our client's business. This role offers stability, hands-on work, and the opportunity to be part of a dedicated manufacturing team.

What you'll be doing

1.	Operating and monitoring production line machinery and equipment to ensure optimal performance
2.	Assembling products according to specifications and quality standards
3.	Inspecting finished products for quality control and identifying any defects or issues
4.	Preparing materials and components for processing stages
5.	Maintaining a clean and safe working environment in compliance with health and safety regulations
6.	Recording production data and reporting any equipment malfunctions or concerns to supervisors
7.	Following standard operating procedures and work instructions accurately
8.	Collaborating with team members to meet production targets and deadlines
9.	Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and providing feedback on processes

What we're looking for

1.	Previous experience in manufacturing, assembly or process work is highly desirable
2.	Ability to work in a fast-paced production environment and meet output targets
3.	Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality standards
4.	Reliability and punctuality, with flexibility to work day and afternoon shifts
5.	Physical capability to perform assembly work and operate machinery safely
6.	Willingness to follow instructions and work as part of a team
7.	Basic literacy and numeracy skills
8.	A valid working visa or Australian citizenship (where applicable)

What we offer

1.	Competitive hourly rates and ongoing employment security
2.	Shift allowances for afternoon shifts
3.	Safe, well-maintained working environment
4.	Opportunity to develop manufacturing and assembly skills
5.	Supportive team environment with experienced supervisors
6.	Career progression opportunities within the organisation
7.	Compliance with all relevant workplace entitlements and condition

Our client is a leading manufacturing company committed to delivering high-quality products and services. They pride themselves on maintaining a skilled workforce, fostering a culture of safety and continuous improvement, and building long-term relationships with their employees. Our clients Moss Vale facility is a hub of production and assembly operations where teamwork and efficiency are at the heart of everything they do. Our client is dedicated to providing a supportive workplace where employees can develop their skills and contribute meaningfully to their success.

Ready to join our team? Apply now to become a Process Worker at Flexiforce Australia.

If you meet the criteria and are ready to start, we want to hear from you ASAP.

The WestMed Basic Physician Training (BPT) Network may offer 1 or 2-year contracts (as required for completion of basic training) to applicants who have completed their time in an accredited BPT role. All other applicants will be offered 3-year contracts, subject to change, with final rankings from the application process and service provision requirements determining the length of training contract that will be offered.

Previous or current registration with the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) in non-BPT roles, does not guarantee a 2-year contract.

Please note that once a BPT offer has been accepted, any application submitted for subsequent-round BPT positions, during the 2027 AMR campaign, will not be considered, for as long as that offer is held.
 

Where you'll be working
The Westmead Hospital is known for its comprehensive and highly specialised services provided to the Western Sydney community, statewide and nationally. Westmead Hospital is a member of the Westmead Health and Education Super Precinct, with close relationships to The Children's Hospital at Westmead, the University of Sydney, the Westmead Institute for Medical Research, and the Children's Medical Research Institute. Currently undergoing a multimillion-dollar rebuilding program, Westmead Hospital with its partners will be one of the largest health, education, research and training precincts in Australia.

The WestMed BPT Network has training positions in Westmead Hospital; Blacktown Hospital; Hornsby Hospital and Orange Hospital. All are teaching hospitals affiliated with Sydney University and UWS. Our metropolitan sites are busy with exposure to a wide variety of presentations and patient populations. Our rural site offers tremendous opportunity to see a diverse range of clinical medicine where you will start to develop the key decision-making and clinical judgement skills of a physician.

Our training program targets your clinical skills and your professional skills. We provide a supportive environment that facilitates your learning and gets you ready to meet the challenges of your career and the RACP exams. We offer a comprehensive program which supplements your own study program, as well as a mentorship program and other learning opportunities. We take education and training seriously and value the same from our trainees.

What you'll be doing
 The primary purpose of the Basic Physician Trainee (BPT) is to provide effective medical services to patients under supervision, while developing expertise in medical practice in a complex clinical environment in inpatient and outpatient areas in the public health organisations within the Network. 
Basic Physician Training roles consist of rotations through medical departments, working under an appropriate level of supervision by consultants. Rotations have different levels of responsibility and team structures. BPTs will gain increasing clinical autonomy and accountability as team leaders throughout the course of the three-year training program, building on their skills and attributes with the goal of entering an Advanced Training program. 
 
BPTs undertaking the care of medical patients should ensure that they operate within their own level of expertise within a collaborative clinical care model and to seek consultation with the treating physician when appropriate, in the following activities:

Clinically assess patients, incorporating consultation-history taking, examination, and formulation of a differential diagnosis and management plans

Discuss diagnoses and management plans with patients and their families or carers

Document the progress of patients in multiple settings

Prescribe medications tailored to patients' needs and conditions

Transfer care of patients

Choose, organise and interpret investigations

Assess and manage acutely unwell patients

Plan, prepare for, perform, and provide after care for important procedures

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Selection Criteria

MBBS or equivalent, current general registration with the Medical Board of Australia

This role requires eligibility for or current registration as a Basic Physician Trainee with the Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) and intent to obtain Fellowship of the RACP. What is your current RACP status?

Demonstrated recent relevant experience in clinical medicine and ability to work in a complex clinical environment with proven ability to apply clinical knowledge and concepts in practical situations. (Limit response to 1500 characters)

Demonstrated teamwork and problem-solving skills within a multidisciplinary team (Limit response to 1500 characters)

Demonstrated time management and prioritisation skills within the context of multiple competing priorities (Limit response to 1500 characters)

Demonstrated commitment to ongoing learning, teaching, research, quality improvement and clinical leadership in medicine (Limit response to 1500 characters)
